verify.note: Closed 2026-09-30 (ADR-1679). Runs the real lib/circles/channels.ts: three Channels save, a Circle stored with them at positions 1..3 is found under each and not under a fourth, the Channel filter reaches a second or third carrier, and a fourth is refused by the save and by the Manage hub add. Then reads the migration (table, position 1..3 plus unique per circle, backfill), the types, the write (positions, and the primary kept on the column), setCircleChannels (checks the cap), listChapters, the Circles index Interest filter, the Channel page, the Channels list counts, and the manifest multiselect. Fails on main (30975a1b0): the migration is gone. Mutation-fired: 9 of 9 arm mutations fail it. Under 0.2 s CPU.

append.detail: CLOSED 2026-09-30 (ADR-1679). PREMISE HELD at 30975a1b0 (main): circles.topical_channel_id was the only link, and the join that once allowed several (circle_topics, 20260604010000) had been dropped as orphaned in 20260925000000. Owner ruling 2026-09-30 ~02:10Z: "Phase it". WHAT SHIPPED: migration 20270345011400_circle_channels.sql adds circle_channels (circle_id, topical_channel_id, position 1..3; primary key (circle_id, topical_channel_id) and unique (circle_id, position), so a fourth row has nowhere to go), backfills every declared Channel as position 1, indexes the Channel FK, and has a public read policy and no write policy (service role only), with a public verdict in scripts/table-grants.txt. lib/database.types.ts carries the table by hand until the next regeneration. Position 1 stays mirrored on circles.topical_channel_id, which the feed and RLS arms keep reading; widening those is LIVE-730 (parked to after launch). The Circle manifest field is now channelIds, a multiselect over the loaded Channels (no kernel change), capped by CIRCLE_MAX_CHANNELS in lib/circles/channels.ts. The Circle settings rail lists the chosen Channels (the first marked Primary), removes any, and adds one more until there are three. The write is setCircleChannels (lib/channels/programs.ts) over writeCircleChannels (lib/circles/channel-carriers.ts), the only write that keeps the column equal to position 1. It refuses a fourth, a missing Circle or Channel, and a paused Channel the Circle does not already carry, and puts the previous list back when an insert fails. startChapter and the Space Program flagship put the Program's Channel first. The Channel Manage hub adds a Circle as one more Channel (a full Circle gets its own notice), and removing one moves the next Channel up. A Channel delete promotes each affected Circle's next Channel. Readers that match ANY of a Circle's Channels: the Circles index Interest filter and counts, the Channel page Circles directory, listChapters, the Channels list counts, the Manage hub list, stat and picker, and the Channel insights count. Everything else stays on the primary by ruling. APPLY the migration to production right before the push (the orchestrator's serial window). Tests: lib/circles/channels.test.ts; lib/channels/programs.test.ts (the closing scenario, the table's cap, paused, restore, add, remove, delete promotion); components/admin/modules/circle-rail-plan.test.ts.
